title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
authors: Gregory Bassen, Wyatt Bunstine, Sarah Okandey, Sarah Cheung, Elaine Flowers, Ritwik Bose
abstract: Although Large Language Models (LLM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools have enabled a rapid increase in the generation rate of predicted materials, the rate of new materials discovery has lagged behind. This is due to the challenges associated with designing a sequence of chemical reactions to predictably produce new materials, especially in new structure types. Here, we report a study of human and LLM generated recipes for the synthesis of known and new materials. The success of the recipes is determined through in-lab experimentation, and the results are passed back to the humans and LLMs in a closed-loop process to study the effects of their collaboration. The Ruddlesden-Popper homologous series was selected for all material candidates to provide a materials phase space that is simultaneously well studied and likely to host undiscovered materials. We find that humans (H) and LLM (L) have similar success rates: 83(8)% (H) and 75(9)% (L) [known materials, round one], 17(9)% (H) and 22(10)% (L) [unknown materials, round one], 79(8)% (H) and 71(9)% (L) [known materials, round two], and 22(7)% (H) and 14(6)% (L) [unknown materials, round two]. Through this collaborative human-LLM effort, we discovered Ba3PtO5, a material with a new structural prototype that constitutes the missing 1D member of the herein reported dimensionally tunable Rock-Salt Perovskite (RSP) homologous series of the form (AX)m(ABX3)p, of which the Ruddlesden-Popper series is a subset.

infographic.key_insight: Human experts and LLMs performed similarly in generating viable materials synthesis recipes, and their closed-loop collaboration helped discover a new material prototype.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The study shows that combining human judgment with LLM-generated synthesis plans can accelerate experimental materials discovery, especially in underexplored compositional spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper candidates using both humans and LLMs.
Tested recipes in the lab and fed results back into a closed-loop collaboration process.
Compared success rates across two rounds to assess learning and discovery performance.
infographic.evidence_signal: In-lab evaluation showed comparable success rates for humans and LLMs on known materials and much lower rates on unknown materials, with a new compound, Ba3PtO5, discovered.
infographic.watch_item: Results are limited by the specific Ruddlesden-Popper phase space and may not directly generalize to other materials families or synthesis constraints.
infographic.paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery

title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
authors: Weikun Zhu, Natalie Ngoh, Shelly Ben-David, Maxwell Conte, Teddy Hsieh, Sarah O. Spector
abstract: Quantum light sources capable of generating single photons are fundamental building blocks for photonic quantum technologies. In the ongoing search for an ideal quantum emitter, inorganic halide perovskite nanocrystals have emerged as a promising source of single photons. Their unique optical response, with an unmatched ease of synthetic tunability, stands out amongst the competing platforms. However, their stochastic dispersion in solution challenges the deterministic and stable integration of individual emitters with photonic structures that is required for practical technologies. Notably, resolution and material compatibility constraints make conventional top-down fabrication processes insufficient for such heterogeneous integration. Here, we report direct writing of perovskite quantum dots (QDs) with individual-emitter resolution. By inducing a nanoscale-confined formation volume using a thermal scanning probe method, we achieve site-selective synthesis down to a single atomic-scale QD with spectral tunability and < 25 nm spatial control. As a result, we demonstrate high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths and high single-photon purity up to 98% at room temperature, performance consistent with that of their state-of-the-art colloidal counterparts. Through such deterministic control, we uniquely realize the precise, on-demand coupling of these emitters to photonic cavities, as evidenced by a measured enhancement in the spontaneous emission rate. This represents a key advancement toward addressing the longstanding integration obstacles of these materials. Overall, by combining the atomic-scale tunability of chemical synthesis with the spatial control of additive manufacturing, our work opens new emitter engineering strategies to realize the untapped potential of colloidal materials for next-generation quantum technologies.

infographic.key_insight: The paper demonstrates deterministic, site-selective direct writing of individual perovskite quantum dots with <25 nm placement control and single-atomic-scale resolution for quantum light emission.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This enables practical integration of high-purity single-photon emitters into photonic devices, overcoming the stochastic placement problem that has limited perovskite-based quantum and optoelectronic architectures.
method: Thermal scanning probe lithography creates a nanoscale-confined formation volume for local QD synthesis.
Direct writing is used to position CsPbI3 quantum dots at designed sites with spectral tunability.
The written emitters are coupled to photonic cavities to verify enhanced spontaneous emission.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths, room-temperature single-photon purity up to 98%, and measured spontaneous-emission enhancement in cavities.
infographic.watch_item: The approach depends on precise thermal scanning probe control and material stability, so scaling to large-area, high-throughput manufacturing may be challenging.
infographic.paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots

title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite
authors: Yuki Takahashi, Daichi Okada, Koshi Oi, Kazuki Mitamura, Takahiko Endo, Yasumitsu Miyata
abstract: Chiral nonlinear optical (NLO) responses enable efficient discrimination of circularly polarized light (CPL) and are attracting increasing interest for optical and optoelectronic technologies. However, studies on NLO properties in chiral materials have largely focused on second-order NLO processes, while the role of chirality in third-order NLO processes remains poorly explored. Here, we demonstrate telecom-band CPL detection by third harmonic generation circular dichroism (THG-CD) in the chiral two-dimensional perovskite (R/S-MBACl)2PbI4 and uncover a giant hidden THG-CD anisotropy that is accessible via polarization-resolved detection. Polarization-resolved THG measurements reveal that opposite chiral NLO responses emerge in orthogonal THG polarization channels. Therefore, these chiral anisotropic contributions largely cancel each other in the total-THG signal detection, leading to underestimation of the THG-CD dissymmetry in conventional evaluations based on total-THG intensity. By separating these hidden chiral contributions, we observe exceptionally large dissymmetry factors exceeding 1.9 and achieve selective extraction of chiral NLO responses with opposite handedness, without any structural chiral inversion. These findings highlight the importance of polarization-resolved analysis for evaluating more accurate chiral NLO responses inherent to the material and provide a promising platform for optical information processing, encryption, and anti-counterfeiting technologies at technologically relevant telecommunication wavelengths.

infographic.key_insight: A chiral 2D halide perovskite can detect telecom-band circularly polarized light through a hidden, giant third-order nonlinear circular dichroism revealed only by polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This points to a route for wavelength-relevant CPL sensing, optical encryption, and anti-counterfeiting devices using perovskite nonlinear optics.
method: Use the chiral 2D perovskite (R/S-MBACl)2PbI4.
Measure polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation in orthogonal output channels.
Compare total-THG vs channel-separated THG to expose hidden opposite-handed chiral responses.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports exceptionally large dissymmetry factors exceeding 1.9 when hidden chiral contributions are separated, whereas conventional total-THG analysis underestimates the effect.
infographic.watch_item: Device performance may look weaker if evaluated only by total THG intensity, so polarization-resolved characterization is essential for correct implementation and comparison.
infographic.paper_title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite

title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
authors: Saba Mahmoodpour, Jiyeon Oh, Yanlin Liu, Zijian Gan, Wei You, Andrew M. Moran
abstract: Non-fullerene acceptors such as Y6 have enabled high-efficiency organic photovoltaic devices and motivated the development of single-component architectures; however, the microscopic mechanisms governing exciton transport and charge dissociation remain under active investigation. In particular, the interplay between Frenkel-charge-transfer excitations and their coupling to environmental fluctuations complicates the description of light absorption and subsequent exciton dynamics. Here, ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy is used to probe exciton quenching dynamics in Y6 films interfaced with hole-transport layers. To interpret these measurements, we develop an analytical model based on hybrid Frenkel-charge-transfer states that enables direct extraction of intermolecular electronic couplings, charge-transfer character, and system-bath interaction strengths from experimental data. The analysis reveals a substantial charge-transfer admixture of 20-40% in the exciton states and identifies a transport regime characterized by delocalization-mediated exciton motion rather than purely diffusive hopping. Consistent with this interpretation, the corresponding quenching dynamics occur on a ~1 ps timescale within ~4 nm of the interface, suggesting a short-range injection mechanism facilitated by exciton delocalization. In addition to providing physical parameters for Y6, these results establish a quantitative framework that connects spectroscopic observables to microscopic transport mechanisms and can be generalized to other non-fullerene acceptors.

infographic.key_insight: Y6 excitons are mixed Frenkel-charge-transfer states with 20–40% charge-transfer character, and their quenching is driven by short-range, delocalization-assisted transport rather than simple hopping.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These results give device designers a quantitative way to link spectroscopy to interfacial transport, helping optimize single-component solar cells and related non-fullerene acceptor architectures.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on Y6 films near hole-transport interfaces.
Analytical hybrid Frenkel-charge-transfer model fit to extract coupling, charge-transfer admixture, and system-bath interaction strengths.
Interpretation of quenching kinetics to infer transport length scale and mechanism.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~1 ps quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, supporting a short-range injection mechanism.
infographic.watch_item: The extracted microscopic parameters are model-dependent, so the conclusions should be validated across film morphologies, interfaces, and other non-fullerene acceptors.
infographic.paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells

title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures
authors: Liudmila Starodubtceva, Ahmed Kadid, Naho Kurahashi, Cedric Kreusel, Jasper Ruhkop, Sebastian Lukas
abstract: Metal halide perovskite semiconductors are promising materials for optoelectronic and photonic devices, including solar cells and next-generation coherent light sources. However, their low thermal conductivity limits the practical operation of devices under high excitation levels. Integrating thermally conductive, large band-gap two-dimensional (2D) materials into perovskite devices could suppress heat accumulation, while preserving their optical properties. Here, we show that planar hot-pressed (PHP) cesium lead bromide (CsPbBr${_3}$) thin films capped with few-layer 2D hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are less affected by laser-induced heating under high-power continuous-wave excitation than uncapped perovskite samples. A large-scale semidry transfer method was developed to integrate 2D hBN onto PHP CsPbBr${_3}$ thin films. The process is chemically and thermally compatible with perovskites. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses show that the hBN capping layer does not alter the morphology and optical properties of the perovskite thin film. The PHP CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN heterostructure exhibits a thermal conductivity of 3 W/(m * K), approximately seven times higher than that of the bare perovskite films of 0.45 W/(m * K). Heat diffusion simulations confirm enhanced heat dissipation in the heterostructure relative to bare perovskite films. Our experiments demonstrate an effective approach to enhancing heat dissipation in perovskite devices using transparent, thermally conductive 2D materials.

infographic.key_insight: Adding few-layer hBN to CsPbBr3 thin films sharply improves heat dissipation without changing the perovskite’s morphology or optical behavior.
infographic.engineering_relevance: A transparent, thermally conductive 2D capping layer can make perovskite optoelectronic devices more stable under high optical or electrical loading.
method: Large-scale semidry transfer of few-layer hBN onto planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 films
Microscopic and spectroscopic characterization to verify unchanged film quality and optics
Heat diffusion simulations to compare capped vs. uncapped thermal behavior
infographic.evidence_signal: The heterostructure shows a measured thermal conductivity of 3 W/(m·K), about 7× higher than bare CsPbBr3 films (0.45 W/(m·K)), and is less affected by laser-induced heating.
infographic.watch_item: Scalability and long-term interface reliability of the hBN/perovskite stack under real device operating conditions still need validation.
infographic.paper_title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures

title: Oxygen-nonstoichiometry-driven phase transition in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-δ}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$) perovskites
authors: Nina Tereshko, Roman Lanovsky, Olivier Toulemonde, Maxim Bushinsky, Stanislav Savvin, Vadim Sikolenko
abstract: We report a systematic study of the interplay between oxygen nonstoichiometry, crystal structure, and magnetic/electrotransport properties in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-δ}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$). High-resolution neutron powder diffraction combined with synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction reveals that increasing the oxygen content induces a structural transition from a layered $I4/mmm$ ($2a_p \times 2a_p \times 4a_p$) to an oxygen-deficient orthorhombic $Pmmm$ ($a_p \times a_p \times 2a_p$) phases with preferential oxygen-vacancy occupation. This transition is accompanied by a crossover from G-type antiferromagnetic with a weak ferromagnetic component to a ferromagnetic state, and a drastic decay in resistivity. The evolution of the magnetic and transport properties is discussed in terms of changes in the Co spin state, enhanced Co $3d$ - O $2p$ orbital overlap upon oxygen uptake, and a magnetically inhomogeneous ferromagnetic state associated with residual oxygen vacancies and mixed $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}/\mathrm{Co}^{4+}$ valence. Our findings experimentally confirm that the stabilization of the layered "314" structure is driven by the presence and ordering of oxygen vacancies rather than A-site cation ordering, whereas the oxygen-deficient oxidized compounds represent an intermediate orthorhombic state preceding fully stoichiometric phases.

infographic.key_insight: In Sr1−xNdxCoO3−δ, adding oxygen triggers a structural shift from layered I4/mmm to oxygen-deficient Pmmm and simultaneously drives a magnetic/transport transition from antiferromagnetic, resistive behavior to ferromagnetic, low-resistance behavior.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Oxygen vacancy control emerges as a practical tuning knob for tailoring cobalt-perovskite phase stability, magnetism, and conductivity in oxide-functional materials.
method: High-resolution neutron powder diffraction
Synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction
Magnetic and electrotransport measurements across x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct structural refinement plus correlated magnetic and resistivity trends showing oxygen-content-driven phase evolution and a drastic resistivity decrease.
infographic.watch_item: The ferromagnetic state is described as magnetically inhomogeneous and vacancy-influenced, so device behavior may depend sensitively on oxygen stoichiometry and defect ordering.
infographic.paper_title: Oxygen-nonstoichiometry-driven phase transition in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-δ}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$) perovskites

title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
authors: Rehmat Sood-Goodwin, Xue-Li Cao, Benjamin C. Kinvig, Robert D. J. Oliver, Yen-Hung Lin, Nic Mullin
abstract: Molecular passivation has become central to reducing photovoltage losses in metal-halide perovskite solar cells, but its electronic action is still often inferred from device-level metrics rather than directly resolved at the nanoscale. Here, we use amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy to examine how [3-(2-aminoethylamino)propyl]trimethoxysilane (AEAPTMS) modifies the surface potential and photovoltage dynamics of mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films. AEAPTMS homogenises the dark contact potential difference (CPD), narrowing its distribution from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV without obvious morphological changes. Under illumination, passivated films show a larger steady-state surface photovoltage (SPV) and faster stabilisation, with the SPV increasing from ~345 to ~417 mV and the stabilisation time constant decreasing from ~840 to ~470 s. Wavelength-dependent SPV further indicates reduced sub-bandgap electronic disorder. By separating grain-boundary and grain-interior contributions, we show that AEAPTMS suppresses grain-boundary potential barriers, linking amino-silane passivation to a more homogeneous and stable carrier landscape.

infographic.key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface potentials more uniform and dynamically stable, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving photovoltage response.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can be used to lower nonradiative losses and improve stability in perovskite solar-cell interfaces.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) and light-induced surface photovoltage (SPV) before and after AEAPTMS passivation
Analyze wavelength-dependent SPV and separate grain-boundary vs grain-interior contributions
infographic.evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD spread from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
infographic.watch_item: These are nanoscale surface measurements on thin films, so device-level performance gains and long-term operational stability still need direct confirmation.
infographic.paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy

title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
authors: Sokipriala Jonah
abstract: Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) can reduce residential electricity costs and support demand response, but adoption is limited by the difficulty of translating household preferences into technical scheduling constraints. This paper evaluates whether large language model (LLM) agents can provide a practical natural-language interface for multi-appliance home energy scheduling. We present a tool-calling ReAct agent that uses live half-hourly Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, photovoltaic generation estimates, household usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base to schedule flexible loads against a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) ground truth. Three commercial models, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6, are benchmarked across tariff days, constraint-conflict scenarios, weather-aware solar co-optimization, and week-long deployment. With native function calling, all models achieve 100% scheduling success and near-MILP optimality, while text-parsed action interfaces sharply reduce reliability. Constraint testing shows that cost-optimal and safety-optimal models differ: Claude is strongest under infeasibility and power-cap conflicts, while GPT-4o-mini is most efficient. Over a simulated week, agents capture 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings, projecting approximately GBP 1,270 annual savings over an off-peak timer baseline. Code and a live demonstration are available at https://github.com/sokistar24/ecohome-energy-agent and https://www.ecohomeagent.com/.

infographic.key_insight: LLM agents can translate household preferences into reliable multi-appliance energy schedules, achieving near-MILP performance when connected to live tools and native function calling.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This work shows a practical path for embedding natural-language control into home energy management systems to reduce electricity costs and improve demand-response automation.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent using live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, photovoltaic estimates, household usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against a MILP ground truth across tariff days, constraint conflicts, and weather-aware solar co-optimization.
Compared native function calling with text-parsed action interfaces, then tested week-long deployment savings against an oracle and off-peak baseline.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across scenarios, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and agents captured 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week, with projected annual savings of about GBP 1,270 versus an off-peak timer baseline.
infographic.watch_item: Performance drops sharply when actions are text-parsed instead of function-called, so robust tool interfaces and constraint handling are essential for real deployments.
infographic.paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management

title: Productive Curtailment in Agrivoltaic Systems under Flexible Interconnection Agreements
authors: Marcus Wu, Anna Stuhlmacher
abstract: Flexible interconnection agreements are increasingly used to streamline the distributed generation interconnection process by limiting real power exports and avoiding costly grid upgrades. Agrivoltaic systems--solar photovoltaic (PV) panels installed over agricultural land--can provide added value under these agreements by adjusting the PV panels away from sun tracking while increasing the sunlight available to crops. This technical note investigates the operation of agrivoltaics under flexible interconnection limits and evaluates their impact on both PV energy production and crop outcomes. We formulate an optimization problem that determines the time-varying tilt of a single-axis tracking agrivoltaic system to maximize energy production subject to a real power export limit over an entire growing season. The resulting PV operating schedules are then used to evaluate PV energy production and crop yield. In a case study, we demonstrate that agrivoltaic systems can comply with flexible interconnection agreements through operational adjustments that improve crop yield, distinguishing them from conventional PV systems that rely solely on inverter curtailment.

infographic.key_insight: Agrivoltaic systems can satisfy flexible interconnection export limits not just by curtailing power, but by re-optimizing panel tilt to preserve energy production while improving crop access to sunlight.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This shows flexible interconnection agreements can be paired with control strategies that turn curtailment constraints into a co-optimization opportunity for PV generation and agricultural performance.
method: Formulated a seasonal optimization problem for single-axis tracking agrivoltaics.
Optimized time-varying tilt to maximize PV energy while enforcing a real power export limit.
Used the resulting operating schedules to assess both PV output and crop-yield implications.
infographic.evidence_signal: A case study over a growing season evaluates the optimized schedules and shows agrivoltaic systems can comply with export limits while improving crop yield.
infographic.watch_item: The approach depends on accurate seasonal optimization and site-specific assumptions, so real-world performance may vary with weather, crop type, tracker hardware, and interconnection rules.
infographic.paper_title: Productive Curtailment in Agrivoltaic Systems under Flexible Interconnection Agreements

title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
authors: Jubair Hossan Abir, Tauhidur Rahman, S. S. B. Pallab, Md. Sharear Aman, R. S. Islam, S. H. Naqib
abstract: In this study, the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties of the novel lead-free halide double perovskite series beta2SnGeX6 (beta = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) are systematically investigated using density functional theory (DFT). Calculated formation energies, Tolerance factors, and octahedral factors confirm that all six compounds exhibit robust thermodynamic stability within a highly symmetric cubic geometry. Mechanical analysis derived from elastic parameters characterizes the entire series as fundamentally ductile, ensuring high processing elasticity and resistance to micro-cracking during device manufacturing. Electronic band structures reveal direct bandgaps showing exceptional composition-dependent tunability from 1.44 eV down to 0.64 eV via progressive halogen substitution. The wide gap chloride variations are optimized for single-junction photovoltaic absorbers, while the narrower-gap bromide and iodide analogs show immense promise for tandem solar architectures and near-infrared photodetectors. Thermoelectrically, heavy constituent atoms introduce strong lattice anharmonicity and intense high-temperature Umklapp phonon scattering, significantly suppressing lattice thermal conductivity. Combined with low carrier effective masses that optimize electrical transport, the iodide compounds achieve higher power factors and outstanding dimensionless figures of merit (ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K). Ultimately, these lead-free double perovskite family emerges as an environmentally benign and versatile platform for next-generation green optoelectronics and solid-state waste-heat recovery.

infographic.key_insight: K/Rb-based lead-free double perovskites β2SnGeX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) are structurally stable, ductile, and strongly tunable from wide- to narrow-bandgap semiconductors for photovoltaics and thermoelectrics.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These materials offer a non-toxic platform for solar absorbers, tandem/NIR optoelectronics, and high-temperature waste-heat recovery, with composition selection controlling bandgap and ZT.
method: DFT-based study of structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Stability screening using formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
Elastic constants, band structures, and transport/phonon-related analysis to assess device suitability
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds are thermodynamically stable and cubic, with direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV and a peak ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
infographic.watch_item: The highest thermoelectric performance is predicted at elevated temperature and from first-principles modeling, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, and defect effects still need validation.
infographic.paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications

title: Sharing Coefficient-Based Price Signals for Demand Response in Renewable Energy Communities
authors: Alireza Shooshtari, Antonio Pepiciello, Jose Luis Dominguez-Garcia
abstract: Renewable energy communities can increase local photovoltaic (PV) use, but feeder-level surplus can still cause reverse power flow in low-voltage networks. Existing sharing coefficient methods are mainly used ex-post for surplus allocation and billing, so they do not directly guide demand toward hours and feeders where shared PV can reduce export. This paper proposes a sharing coefficient-based demand response framework that converts dynamic proportional allocation outcomes into household specific day-ahead price signals. The feeder-aware design first shares surplus within each feeder, while the feeder-agnostic design shares surplus through a single community pool. The energy community manager iteratively computes the allocation from submitted demand and PV forecasts, decomposes purchased energy into same-feeder, inter-feeder, and grid-import components, and coordinates household load reshaping through a convex optimization model. Using measured profiles from 15 households and AC power flow analysis, the framework reduces feeder reverse energy by 45.0% and 44.6% on selected high reverse energy days, and by 69.0% and 66.3% over the annual window, for the feeder-aware and feeder-agnostic cases, respectively. These results show that sharing coefficients can be used not only for ex-post billing, but also as operational price signals for demand response, with feeder-aware allocation providing an additional network benefit by accounting for household location in the low-voltage network.

infographic.key_insight: Sharing coefficients can be turned from an ex-post billing rule into day-ahead price signals that steer household demand toward locally useful PV surplus and cut reverse power flow.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical demand-response control layer for low-voltage renewable energy communities, with feeder-aware pricing adding network value by respecting where loads and PV are connected.
method: Compute dynamic sharing coefficients from forecast demand and PV to allocate surplus energy.
Translate allocated energy into household-specific day-ahead price signals.
Use a convex optimization model to reshape loads; compare feeder-aware vs feeder-agnostic community sharing.
infographic.evidence_signal: Using measured profiles from 15 households with AC power flow analysis, the approach reduced feeder reverse energy by up to 45.0% and 44.6% on selected days and by 69.0% and 66.3% over the annual window.
infographic.watch_item: Performance depends on accurate forecasts, household participation, and communication/optimization infrastructure, so real-world adoption may be sensitive to forecast error and user responsiveness.
infographic.paper_title: Sharing Coefficient-Based Price Signals for Demand Response in Renewable Energy Communities

title: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Solar PV Panel Fault Classification
authors: Seyyedhamid Azimidokht, Mehdi Monemi, Abdelhak Kharbouch, Farid Hamzehaghdam, Mehdi Rasti, Jamshid Aghaei
abstract: The rapid expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems has increased the need for reliable and scalable fault classification, as manual inspection is impractical at scale. Thermal infrared (IR) imaging provides a non-contact solution for identifying PV faults; however, accurate classification remains challenging due to class imbalance, limited texture information, and subtle thermal differences. In this work, we investigate the applicability of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) for thermal IR PV fault classification across various scenarios and propose JEFFNet (JEPA-EFFicientNet), a multibranch architecture that combines JEPA-based self-supervised representation learning with EfficientNetV2-S-based supervised convolutional feature extraction. JEFFNet fuses semantic representations from a JEPA-pretrained Vision Transformer with convolutional features from EfficientNetV2-S, enabling complementary feature learning. JEFFNet is evaluated on two public thermal IR datasets, PVF-10 and InfraredSolarModules (ISM), for both multiclass and derived binary (healthy/faulty) classification. On PVF-10, JEFFNet achieves an F1-score of $93.21$ and an accuracy of $94.33$ in the 10-class task, and an F1-score of $97.53$ and an accuracy of $96.41$ in the derived 2-class task. On ISM, JEFFNet achieves an F1-score of $72.60$ and an accuracy of $83.88$ in the 12-class task, and an F1-score of $94.69$ and an accuracy of $94.78$ in the derived 2-class task. JEFFNet also uses only 108.6M parameters versus 205.91M for GEPFNet, a 47.2\% reduction. These results demonstrate that combining self-supervised semantic and supervised convolutional features provides an effective, parameter-efficient solution for thermal IR PV fault classification. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Azimi2kht/JEFFNet

infographic.key_insight: JEFFNet combines self-supervised JEPA representations with EfficientNetV2-S features to improve thermal IR solar PV fault classification while reducing model size.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable, parameter-efficient path for automated PV inspection using non-contact infrared imaging, which is valuable for large solar farms where manual review is impractical.
method: Pretrain a Vision Transformer with JEPA for semantic representation learning from thermal IR images.
Extract complementary supervised convolutional features with EfficientNetV2-S.
Fuse both branches in a multibranch JEFFNet classifier for multiclass and binary fault detection.
infographic.evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on PVF-10 and InfraredSolarModules, achieving up to 94.33% accuracy on PVF-10 (10-class) and 94.78% accuracy on ISM (2-class), with 108.6M parameters versus 205.91M for GEPFNet.
infographic.watch_item: Performance is lower on the more difficult ISM multiclass task, so class imbalance, limited texture cues, and dataset shift may still affect real-world deployment.
infographic.paper_title: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Solar PV Panel Fault Classification

title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
authors: Ho Truong Nam Hai, Augusto Ducati Luchessi, Makoto Arita, Qixin Guo, Kaveh Edalati
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 conversion driven by solar energy is a highly promising approach in addressing rising atmospheric CO2 levels; however, its practical application remains limited by low conversion efficiency. In this study, a new strategy to enhance CO2 reduction toward CO and CH4 is proposed through the employment of microalgae as a sacrificial agent, and the efficiency is compared with conventional CO2 conversion without and with the use of microplastics as sacrificial agents. To realize this strategy, an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide (HEO), (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with bi-polymorphy of layered perovskite and pyrochlore, is rationally designed. The HEO incorporates alkali metal cesium and alkaline earth metal barium to increase surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption, bismuth with its stereochemically active lone pairs for localized polarization and charge separation, and tantalum and niobium to form octahedral crystalline frameworks for charge transport. The utilization of microalgae during photocatalytic reactions leads to a remarkable enhancement in CO2 conversion compared to catalysis with or without using microplastics, with CO and CH4 production increasing by 10- and 4-fold, respectively, compared to the system using only HEO. These findings not only demonstrate a new family of polymorphic AB2-type HEOs for photocatalysis but also show the potential of microalgae as a sustainable sacrificial agent, offering an environmentally friendly pathway for efficient CO2 capture (through photosynthesis by microalgae) and CO2 conversion (through photocatalysis by HEOs).

infographic.key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial agent substantially boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The study points to a scalable, more sustainable pathway for carbon capture and conversion by pairing catalyst design with a carbon-negative biological scavenger.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type HEO: (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6
Leveraged layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy to improve charge transport and separation
Used microalgae during photocatalysis and compared performance against no scavenger and microplastics
infographic.evidence_signal: Compared with HEO-only catalysis, adding microalgae increased CO production about 10-fold and CH4 production about 4-fold, outperforming systems with or without microplastics.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not report long-term stability, reactor scalability, or the practical logistics of integrating living microalgae with photocatalytic operation.
infographic.paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger

title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
authors: Francesco Lodola, Zhuangyi Zhou, Boaz Koren, Saeed Bayat, Alessandro Magon, Yucheng Hu
abstract: Among the highly efficient photovoltaic technologies, that do not rely on epitaxy, only chalcopyrites have a bandgap tunable down to 1.00 eV, the ideal for tandem applications. This is obtained with a pure CuInSe2 absorber without Ga. GaOx has been shown to be an efficient hole transport layer that prevents recombination at the metallic back contact. On the other hand, GaOx has proven detrimental, when it forms on In containing transparent back contacts in bifacial solar cells. Here, we investigate the conditions that make the GaOx layer conductive. We employ a GaOx hole transport layer that is formed through ion exchange during co-evaporation of the low band gap absorber layer. We find that no additional Cu is needed, and that Na is not necessary for a conductive GaOx. Nor did we find a systematic influence of oxygen flow during the sputtering process of the oxide layer. The GaOx layer is partly crystalline. The optimized passivating hole transport layer enables a CuInSe2 bottom solar cell, without any addition of Ag or heavy alkalis, with an active area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage VOC of 552meV

infographic.key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer can be formed by ion exchange during CuInSe2 co-evaporation, enabling low-bandgap bottom cells with high VOC and strong efficiency without extra Cu, Na, Ag, or heavy alkalis.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells that supports tandem PV integration while simplifying process chemistry.
method: Form GaOx during absorber co-evaporation via ion exchange.
Test whether Cu addition, Na, and O2 sputter flow affect GaOx conductivity.
Optimize the passivating hole transport layer in a CuInSe2 solar cell stack.
infographic.evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved over 16% active-area efficiency and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV.
infographic.watch_item: The conductive behavior appears sensitive to how GaOx forms and crystallizes, so transferability to other back-contact stacks or fabrication lines may require re-optimization.
infographic.paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?

title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
authors: P. Dhariwal, D. Prakash, K. D. Verma, A. Kumari, P. K. Kamlesh, A. S. Verma
abstract: Herein, the fundamental physical characteristics like structural, electronic, optical parameters of the Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) materials have been investigated for their potential optoelectronic applications, particularly for solar cells and related devices. To the crystallographic investigations, Ca$_3$PI$_3$ has the most stable configuration among all investigated materials. From the band structure analyses of these materials indicate that all materials have a direct bandgap in the range of 2.0 eV to 3.788 eV, which makes them ideal for light absorption. For the photovoltaic applications, we have analysed first-principles spectroscopic screening limited maximum efficiency (SLME) which confirms that the Ca$_3$PI$_3$ material exhibits the highest solar cell efficiency 29.6% and Ca$_3$PF$_3$ and shows lower efficiency for solar cell suitability 0.6%. Thus, these results demonstrate the real potential and abilities of halide substitution to tune the materials for particular optoelectronic devices.

infographic.key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 strongly tunes bandgap and photovoltaic performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the most promising solar absorber.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The results identify composition control as a practical design lever for optimizing perovskite-inspired materials for next-generation photovoltaic devices.
method: First-principles calculations of structural and electronic properties
Optical property analysis to assess light-absorption potential
SLME screening to estimate solar cell efficiency
infographic.evidence_signal: All four compounds were predicted to have direct bandgaps (2.0–3.788 eV), and SLME ranked Ca3PI3 highest at 29.6% while Ca3PF3 was lowest at 0.6%.
infographic.watch_item: The reported efficiencies come from computational screening, so experimental stability, synthesis feasibility, and device integration still need validation.
infographic.paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency

title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
authors: Chadawan Khamdang, Mengen Wang
abstract: Halide perovskites show great promise for applications in optoelectronic devices. The lead-free perovskites are attracting increasing interest due to their low toxicity and motivate the exploration of alternative compositions and structures, including A$_2$BX$_6$, A$_2$BB$^\prime$X$_6$, A$_3$B$_2$X$_9$, and A$_4$BX$_6$. Accurate predictions of a wide range of band gap energies are important for designing new materials. It is also desired to generate a direct relationship between the structural and elemental descriptors and the band gap energies. In this work, we develop machine learning models to predict band gap energies across various types of halide perovskites based on atomic and structural properties. Algorithms including ensemble tree-based methods, random forest regression (RFR), gradient boosted regression trees (GBRT), and extreme gradient boosting (XGB) showed strong predictive accuracy. We also analyzed feature importance to identify key descriptors, including B-site and X-site elemental properties, as well as the number of A- and B-site atoms, as primary factors influencing band gap energies. These results improve our understanding of the ML models and provide guidance for designing new halide perovskite materials.

infographic.key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict band gaps across diverse halide perovskite families using simple atomic and structural descriptors, with B-site and X-site chemistry emerging as the strongest drivers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These models help screen lead-free perovskite compositions faster, guiding materials design for optoelectronic devices and solar-cell optimization.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors: Random Forest, GBRT, and XGBoost
Used atomic and structural descriptors from multiple halide perovskite types
Interpreted feature importance to connect composition with band gap behavior
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across several halide perovskite compositions and consistent feature-importance patterns highlighting key descriptors.
infographic.watch_item: Model reliability may depend on the diversity and quality of the training data, so predictions should be validated before using them to propose new compositions.
infographic.paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites

title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction
authors: Hang Fan, Weican Liu, Ying Lu, Dunnan Liu, Long Cheng, Wei Wei
abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for reliable grid dispatch and renewable energy integration, yet it remains challenging because PV generation is jointly shaped by weather variability, day-night transitions, regime-dependent dynamics, and strict physical constraints. We propose PARA-PV, a Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented framework that embeds physical knowledge throughout the forecasting process. The framework first encodes multivariate PV observations into patch-level representations and, through a physics-aware retrieval-augmented learner, retrieves historical patches and analog trajectories that are consistent with the current window in temporal shape, power level, PV operating state, and intra-day period; this yields a physically grounded base forecast. To supplement local memory with broader temporal knowledge, the base forecast is then calibrated against a frozen Chronos time-series foundation-model prior through a lightweight residual adapter, so that general temporal regularities are adapted to PV-specific dynamics without overriding the physically grounded prediction. Because residual conditional distribution shifts persist when weather and diurnal regimes change, a physics-aware distribution shift correction module subsequently adjusts the preliminary forecast using power, weather, timestamp, and day/night conditions, applying gated mean-shift and scale corrections selectively. Finally, a physics-constrained loss function partitions the samples into peak, ramping, night-time, and regular regimes and adaptively reweights their error contributions, preventing the dominant regular regime from suppressing learning of operationally critical states. Our code is available at https://github.com/weican1103/PARA-PV.

infographic.key_insight: PARA-PV improves photovoltaic forecasting by combining physics-aware retrieval, a frozen foundation-model prior, and distribution-shift correction to better handle weather, day-night transitions, and regime changes.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The method can support more reliable grid dispatch and renewable integration by producing forecasts that respect PV operating physics while adapting to changing conditions.
method: Retrieves historical patches and analogous trajectories matched by temporal shape, power level, PV state, and intra-day period to build a physically grounded base forecast.
Uses a frozen Chronos foundation model with a lightweight residual adapter to inject broad temporal priors without overriding PV-specific behavior.
Applies physics-aware distribution-shift correction plus a regime-weighted loss to handle peak, ramping, night-time, and regular conditions.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract describes a PV forecasting framework evaluated for accuracy under weather variability and regime shifts, with a publicly available code release for reproducibility.
infographic.watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of historical retrieval and the correctness of the shift-correction gates, which could be sensitive to site-specific data and missing weather/operating signals.
infographic.paper_title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction

title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
authors: Ian T. Vidamour, Fernando Aguirre, Thomas J. Hayward, Matthew O. A. Ellis, Charles Swindells, Alexander McDonnell
abstract: Physical neural networks promise low-power machine learning by computing directly with analogue device physics, but most architectures force nonlinear device responses to act as scalar weights. Inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, we place trainable nonlinear functions on the connections, making each physical connection a learnable computational element. Realising these functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays, we find that the benefit is task-dependent and follows from the smoothness of the physical basis: the networks represent smooth, continuously valued targets, including robotic kinematics, continuous control, and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, with far fewer nodes and connections than multilayer perceptrons, but offer no parameter-efficiency advantage on classification-like decision boundaries. Trained networks transfer to hardware across approximately 35,000 connections with quantified fidelity, and a dedicated CMOS implementation is projected to operate at approximately 30 microwatts. A memristive realisation reproduces the same behaviour in simulation, indicating that the advantage comes from placing trainable nonlinearity on connections, rather than from a particular device.

infographic.key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on connections, rather than using devices only as scalar weights, makes analogue neural networks more efficient for smooth continuous-control problems.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-power hardware path for robotic control, kinematics, and photovoltaic tracking using physically implemented, trainable analogue circuits.
method: Implemented connection-wise nonlinear functions as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Compared the architecture against multilayer perceptrons on smooth targets and decision-boundary-like tasks.
Projected a dedicated CMOS version and also simulated a memristive realisation to test device-agnostic behavior.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the networks used far fewer nodes and connections on smooth continuous tasks, transferred across roughly 35,000 connections with quantified fidelity, and were projected to run at about 30 microwatts in CMOS.
infographic.watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and does not appear for classification-like decision boundaries, so the approach is not universally parameter-efficient.
infographic.paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control

title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
authors: Ana B. Cristóbal, Daniel Sierra, Laura Palomino, Luis Miguel Carrasco, Luis Narvarte
abstract: The success of distributed photovoltaics may be undermining its own future. As solar penetration increases, electricity prices decline during periods of peak generation, reducing the value of surplus photovoltaic production. This raises a critical question: can citizen-led energy systems remain economically viable in electricity markets dominated by renewable generation? Rather than exploring technically optimal but institutionally unrealistic solutions, we examine the options available under current regulatory and market conditions. Using high-resolution consumption data from a rural community sharing a PV facility among 24 users, we identify pathways for long-term sustainability. The study makes two contributions. First, it shows that effective internal coordination can mobilize participation and investment as successfully as external subsidies. Second, it compares static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing models, with and without storage, providing a flexible framework that balances efficiency, fairness, and governance. Results show that collective self-consumption reduces required PV capacity, lowers investment costs, and increases annual savings compared with individually operated systems. Alternative allocation schemes further improve benefit distribution and local electricity use, although gains depend on trade-offs between efficiency, fairness, and governance complexity. Under current electricity prices and remuneration schemes, battery storage provides limited additional economic value and becomes attractive only under specific market conditions. Overall, the long-term viability of citizen-led photovoltaic initiatives depends less on technological sophistication than on collective coordination and adaptive governance.

infographic.key_insight: Under declining electricity prices and weak surplus remuneration, shared photovoltaic self-consumption stays viable mainly through collective coordination and adaptive energy-sharing rules rather than through more complex technology alone.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For community PV systems, designing governance, allocation, and sizing strategies can matter more economically than adding storage, especially when market incentives for exported solar power are low.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural PV-sharing community with 24 users.
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing models, both with and without battery storage.
Evaluated efficiency, fairness, governance complexity, investment cost, and annual savings under current market conditions.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowers required PV capacity and investment costs while increasing annual savings versus individual operation, whereas battery storage adds limited value except in specific price and remuneration conditions.
infographic.watch_item: Results depend strongly on local tariff structures, surplus compensation rules, and the governance capacity of the user group, which may limit transferability.
infographic.paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation

title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
authors: Ethan R. Cronk, Wenjun Xiang, Rachel Fister, Biswajit Ball, Feng Yan, Liping Yu
abstract: Cesium lead chloride (CsPbCl3) is a well known and principal model for inorganic perovskite halide optoelectronic research. The many available techniques including high temperature stability testing have been used to investigate the increasing interest in inorganic perovskites as primary layers in solar cell applications. Due to the nature of high temperature testing, the characterization technique, reproducibility, and the true sample temperature are vital in determining relative stability. By choosing CsPbCl3 in the investigation of the structural stability of perovskites at high temperatures, it acts as a baseline to create and verify a methodology that accurately probes sample temperature, phase transitions, and decomposition onsets. Therefore, we present a methodological approach to investigate the thermal interactions and stability of CsPbCl3 as a parent single perovskite halide based on ligand-assisted re-precipitation synthesis techniques. Where we use our approach to inform and probe thermal interactions in other cesium/chlorine compounds like Cs2AgSbCl6. By analyzing the stoichiometry and initial phases through investigations of the crystalline structure and particle morphology, we calculated temperature conversions using a control substrate and refinements to best estimate changing structure parameters. Using in-situ temperature dependent X-ray diffraction, we were able to effectively probe the phase transitions and decomposition temperatures of the investigated halide powders. Creating a process that can confirm known high temperature structural phenomena of model perovskite halides while verifying our true sample temperature. Which allowed for further testing on the thermal kinetics of on the double perovskite structure Cs2AgSbCl6 and will continue to allow us to test other perovskites and perovskite families of interest in modern high temperature perovskite halide research.

infographic.key_insight: The paper establishes a temperature-calibrated in-situ XRD workflow to more accurately measure phase stability and decomposition in cesium halide perovskites, using CsPbCl3 as a benchmark and Cs2AgSbCl6 as a test case.
infographic.engineering_relevance: This improves the reliability of thermal stability screening for inorganic perovskite solar-cell materials by separating true sample behavior from furnace or substrate temperature error.
method: Ligand-assisted re-precipitation synthesis of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 powders
In-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction to track phase transitions and decomposition
Control-substrate-based temperature conversion/refinement to estimate true sample temperature
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports structural characterization, morphology analysis, and in-situ XRD observations that identified phase transitions and decomposition temperatures for the investigated halide powders.
infographic.watch_item: Thermal conclusions depend on accurate temperature calibration and may vary with heating setup, substrate coupling, and sample morphology.
infographic.paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
